title: Can AI Understand a Distressed Credit? - Harneet Kaur, Axim Intelligence
talk_summary: A distressed-credit investor describes testing whether frontier LLMs can 'understand' a live distressed credit (iHeartMedia), finding that raw models disagree wildly on outcome probabilities but converge once forced through a structured, layered reasoning process (extraction → derivation → judgment → prediction). The core transferable idea is decomposing a hard judgment task into verifiable layers and benchmarking each layer separately before trusting the final prediction.

takeaways.technique: Layer-wise benchmarking of a reasoning pipeline
takeaways.what_they_do: They break the analysis into distinct layers (extraction, reconciliation/derivation, judgment, prediction) and benchmark the model at each layer separately, because 'at each layer the LLM could mess up' and a bad lower layer poisons the final judgment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we benchmark each layer. So, obviously these are at each layer the LLM could mess up

takeaways.technique: Structured reasoning scaffold to force model convergence
takeaways.what_they_do: When two strong models were given the same raw context they disagreed (62% vs 25% bankruptcy); after imposing an explicit structured reasoning process, both converged to ~25% and the same most-likely path.
takeaways.numbers: 62% vs 25% bankruptcy before; both ~25% after scaffolding

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat divergence between two strong models on the same context as a flag that the reasoning is under-specified, then use convergence after scaffolding as evidence the process is sound.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they disagreed. Like they disagreed on what the probabilities of the future would be

takeaways.technique: Separate extraction from derivation from judgment
takeaways.what_they_do: They note extraction is 'pretty solved' for clean public data but hard for messy PDFs/Excel, and that derivation (computing leverage from EBITDA+debt) is a distinct step from judgment — keeping them separate prevents compounding errors.
takeaways.evidence_quote: extraction would be you got EBITDA. Uh derivation would be, okay, now you have EBITDA and you have debt
